## The question

[Example of system architecture picture in TikZ](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/19941/example-of-system-architecture-picture-in-tikz), asked by [Skarab](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/4441/skarab) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-06-05; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I am looking for an example of a system architecture diagram in TikZ. I would like to draw a picture similar to this one:
> ![][q-1]
>
> Therefore I search for existing shapes for: *cloud* (Current State), *database* and *document collection* (Confs) or a way to learn how to draw them.
>
>
>   [q-1]: ulijM.gif
:::

The `cloud` and the `cylinder` are in the shape libraries.  See Sections 48.3 and 48.4 of the TikZ 2.10 manual.

The document collection shape you'll have to put together yourself, though. You can super-impose rectangles and then a `tape` shape on top of that.
